beats.label: S1 · Slayer arrives on the Hellmouth
beats.text: Buffy transfers to Sunnydale hoping to leave slaying behind, but her new Watcher Giles reveals the town sits on a Hellmouth attracting demons.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the premise, Buffy's reluctance, and the town's role that anchors every future season.

beats.label: S1 · The core circle forms
beats.text: Willow and Xander are pulled into her secret after a vampire attack, and a mysterious ally named Angel begins feeding Buffy cryptic warnings.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the Scooby dynamic and Angel, whose identity drives later arcs.

beats.label: S1 · Angel's secret
beats.text: After a kiss, Angel reveals himself as a vampire cursed with a soul for centuries of atrocities, and the two agree they cannot be together.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up Angel's cursed-soul rule, the load-bearing constraint for every romance beat that follows.

beats.label: S1 · The Anointed One rises
beats.text: A prophecy names a child, Collin, who will free the imprisoned Master, and he quietly takes his place at the ancient vampire's side.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names the vessel that will free the Master, driving the finale.

beats.label: S1 · The prophecy of death
beats.text: Giles uncovers a prophecy that the Slayer will die facing the Master; Buffy overhears, quits, then walks to her fate anyway.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The choice that defines Buffy as a hero and triggers the mechanic that creates a second Slayer.

beats.label: S1 · Death and resurrection
beats.text: The Master drains Buffy and escapes his prison, but Xander revives her with CPR and she returns to impale him on shattered wood.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Buffy's brief death is the mechanic that will call the next Slayer, a plot engine for season 2.

beats.label: S1 · Joyce still in the dark
beats.text: Buffy hides everything from her mother Joyce, who thinks she is just a delinquent daughter starting to straighten out.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The unresolved secret between Buffy and Joyce sets up the domestic tension that runs through later seasons.

cliffhanger.text: The Master is dead and the Hellmouth is quiet, but Buffy died for a moment during the fight, and the vampire hierarchy of Sunnydale has been left leaderless with the Anointed One still around.
questions: What happens to a Slayer who technically died and came back?
Who steps into the power vacuum the Master leaves behind?
Can Buffy and Angel keep their distance now that they have both admitted their feelings?

characters.name: Buffy Summers
characters.line: The Slayer, sixteen, briefly killed by the Master and now trying to live a normal high-school life in a town that will not let her.

characters.name: Rupert Giles
characters.line: Sunnydale High's librarian and Buffy's Watcher, trainer and researcher, a stiff Englishman quietly devoted to her.

characters.name: Willow Rosenberg
characters.line: Buffy's shy, brilliant best friend, the group's researcher, quietly in love with Xander.

characters.name: Xander Harris
characters.line: Buffy's loyal friend who resuscitated her at the finale; carries an unspoken crush on Buffy.

characters.name: Angel
characters.line: A brooding vampire cursed with a soul, in love with Buffy but keeping his distance because of what he is.

characters.name: Joyce Summers
characters.line: Buffy's mother, recently divorced, unaware her daughter is the Slayer and still treating her as a troubled teen.

characters.name: Cordelia Chase
characters.line: Popular, cutting classmate who briefly helped in the finale but remains on the edges of the group.
characters.note: Peripheral at end of S1; becomes more entwined in S2.

characters.name: The Anointed One (Collin)
characters.line: A child vampire, quiet successor to the Master, now the highest-ranking vampire left in Sunnydale.

beats.label: S2 · Spike and Drusilla arrive
beats.text: Two lovers roll into Sunnydale: Spike, a punk vampire who has killed two Slayers, and his fragile, prophetic sire Drusilla, who is dying.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the two antagonists who dominate the season and remain load-bearing figures afterward.

beats.label: S2 · A second Slayer is called
beats.text: Because Buffy briefly died the previous year, another Slayer, Kendra, is called and briefly fights alongside her before returning home.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the two-Slayers rule and Kendra's line of succession, which the finale exploits.

beats.label: S2 · Buffy and Angel sleep together
beats.text: On her seventeenth birthday, Buffy and Angel consummate their relationship, and the moment of perfect happiness breaks the Romani curse holding his soul.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The pivot of the season — the mechanic that turns Angel into the villain.

beats.label: S2 · Angelus returns
beats.text: Souless once more, Angelus joins Spike and Drusilla and begins a personal campaign to break Buffy, tormenting her, her mother, and her friends.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Recasts the season's love interest as its Big Bad; the emotional core of everything that follows.

beats.label: S2 · Jenny is murdered
beats.text: Computer teacher Jenny Calendar, secretly a Romani sent to watch Angel, translates the soul-restoring curse, and Angelus snaps her neck and leaves her in Giles's bed.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Motivates Giles's rage and preserves the curse text, which becomes the finale's linchpin.

beats.label: S2 · Spike defects
beats.text: Crippled and sidelined by Angelus's affair with Drusilla, Spike offers Buffy an alliance to stop Angelus from ending the world so he can keep it.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Marks the first crack in Spike's villainy and his split from Drusilla, foundational for his later status.

beats.label: S2 · Buffy sends Angel to hell
beats.text: Willow restores Angel's soul mid-battle, but the ritual is already open; Buffy kisses him, then runs him through with a sword to close the portal.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's final image and the reason Buffy flees Sunnydale, which shapes every relationship in S3.

beats.label: S2 · Buffy runs
beats.text: Expelled by Snyder, outed as the Slayer to Joyce, and wanted by police for Kendra's murder, Buffy leaves town without a word to anyone.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The state everyone is in at the start of S3 — Joyce knows, Sunnydale is broken, Buffy is gone.

cliffhanger.text: Buffy has stabbed a re-souled Angel into a hell dimension and vanished from Sunnydale, leaving her friends without a Slayer, her mother knowing the truth for the first time, and Kendra dead in the library.
questions: Where does Buffy go, and can she come back from what she just did?
Now that Kendra is dead, will another Slayer be called in her place?
How do Joyce and the Scoobies rebuild after learning everything and losing her?

characters.name: Buffy Summers
characters.line: Just killed the man she loved to save the world, expelled and wanted for murder, and has run away from Sunnydale.

characters.name: Angel / Angelus
characters.line: Restored to his soul at the last second, then stabbed by Buffy through a portal to hell.

characters.name: Rupert Giles
characters.line: Grieving Jenny, tortured by Angelus, and left without a Slayer to guide.

characters.name: Willow Rosenberg
characters.line: Recovering from a coma; discovered real magical talent when she cast the soul curse and is dating werewolf Oz.

characters.name: Xander Harris
characters.line: Now in a bickering, secret-turned-open relationship with Cordelia; withheld from Buffy that Willow was trying the curse.

characters.name: Cordelia Chase
characters.line: Reluctantly part of the group, dating Xander after their basement kiss.

characters.name: Oz
characters.line: Willow's boyfriend, a laconic guitarist who is also a werewolf three nights a month.

characters.name: Joyce Summers
characters.line: Finally told that Buffy is the Slayer, and left alone in the house after ordering her not to come back if she leaves.

characters.name: Spike
characters.line: Left Sunnydale with a healed Drusilla after helping Buffy against Angelus; back on his feet, out of the game for now.

characters.name: Principal Snyder
characters.line: The petty, Hellmouth-aware principal who expelled Buffy from Sunnydale High.

beats.label: S3 · Buffy comes home
beats.text: After hiding in Los Angeles under the name Anne, Buffy returns to Sunnydale and slowly repairs things with a wounded Joyce and her angry friends.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Resets the board after her S2 exit and re-establishes the domestic status quo the season builds on.

beats.label: S3 · Faith arrives
beats.text: A second Slayer, Faith, called by Kendra's death, turns up in Sunnydale — reckless, hungry for the work, and jealous of Buffy's life.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the season's shadow-Buffy, the character whose slide drives everything after the midpoint.

beats.label: S3 · Angel returns, kept secret
beats.text: Angel claws back from hell, feral and mute; Buffy nurses him in secret and hides his return from the group, especially Giles.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The lie that fractures the group's trust when it comes out, and re-opens the impossible romance.

beats.label: S3 · The Mayor and Mr. Trick
beats.text: Sunnydale's cheerful Mayor Richard Wilkins is revealed as a century-old sorcerer preparing an Ascension into a pure demon, recruiting vampire Mr. Trick to help him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names the season's Big Bad and the endgame ritual everything else is racing toward.

beats.label: S3 · Faith crosses the line
beats.text: Faith accidentally stakes Deputy Mayor Allan, feels the thrill more than the guilt, and tries to pin it on Buffy before Giles sees through her.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The break that pushes Faith to the Mayor's side and creates the Slayer-vs-Slayer axis of the finale.

beats.label: S3 · Faith joins the Mayor
beats.text: After Faith kills Mr. Trick to save Buffy, she walks into the Mayor's office and offers to replace him as his enforcer; he takes her in like a daughter.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Completes Faith's defection and establishes the parental bond that makes the finale personal.

beats.label: S3 · Angel leaves
beats.text: Told by Joyce and himself that he is holding Buffy back, Angel breaks it off and quietly decides to leave Sunnydale after the Ascension.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up his departure and the emotional cost of the finale even if he survives it.

beats.label: S3 · Graduation
beats.text: Faith poisons Angel and slips into a coma after Buffy stabs her; the class arms itself, the Mayor ascends into the demon Olvikan, and Giles blows up the school with him inside.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The end of high school, the school itself, and the Mayor arc — the state the group starts S4 from.

cliffhanger.text: The Mayor and Sunnydale High are rubble, Faith is in a coma no one expects her to wake from, and the class scatters — Cordelia and Wesley gone, Angel walking away without a goodbye, and Buffy standing in the ash of the only life she has ever had.
questions: What do a Slayer and her friends do once the school and the enemy are both gone?
Will Faith wake up, and what happens to her if she does?
Can Buffy build any kind of life now that Angel has left and everyone is moving on?

characters.name: Buffy Summers
characters.line: High-school graduate, single after Angel's departure, freshly out from under the Watchers' Council after quitting to save him.

characters.name: Rupert Giles
characters.line: Fired by the Council for caring about Buffy; still her mentor, no longer her official Watcher, and the man who lit the fuse on the school.

characters.name: Willow Rosenberg
characters.line: Serious about witchcraft now, sleeping with Oz, and planning to stay in Sunnydale for college rather than leave.

characters.name: Xander Harris
characters.line: Not going to college; slept with Faith once and got dumped, broke up with Cordelia after being caught kissing Willow.

characters.name: Oz
characters.line: Willow's steady boyfriend and part-time werewolf, now the group's calm center.

characters.name: Angel
characters.line: Back from hell, broke up with Buffy for her own good, and left town after the graduation battle.

characters.name: Faith
characters.line: The rogue second Slayer, adopted by the Mayor, stabbed by Buffy and left in a coma no one knows how long will last.

characters.name: Joyce Summers
characters.line: Now fully aware of Buffy's life, uneasy but supportive, and the one who quietly told Angel to leave.

characters.name: Mayor Richard Wilkins
characters.line: Sunnydale's folksy mayor and century-old sorcerer, dead — blown up as the demon Olvikan inside the school library.
